answers_by_date.basis: In force: DL 1.094 (1975) and DS 597 (1984). Neither stops private persons such as employers from keeping a migrant's identity documents. The only retention clauses (DS 597 arts. 7 and 70) let the maritime and border authorities hold travel documents. The Código del Trabajo has no such rule either. No practice evidence for this period.
Same regime as in 2000. No relevant amendment to DL 1.094 or DS 597, and no practice evidence.

Same regime. Ley 20.430 (April 2010) came after this date and does not deal with private retention. The CMW's 2011 Concluding Observations describe the authorities taking documents under the Alien Act (replaced by an 'Alien Offender Card'). That is state retention, not a protection.

Ley 20.507 (8 April 2011) created the trafficking offence and added art. 33 bis to DL 1.094 (temporary residence for victims). It did not ban the retention of documents by private persons. Nothing else changed before 2020.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been no right protections neither in 2000 nor in 2020

answers.repealed_search: Searched the consolidated DL 1.094 and DS 597 on LeyChile for 'retención', 'retener', 'retendr' and 'infractor'. The only retention clauses found allow authorities to hold travel documents (DS 597 arts. 7 and 70). A web search for any Código del Trabajo rule or Dirección del Trabajo dictamen against employers keeping passports found none. Ley 20.507 contains no such ban. No earlier protection was found that had been repealed or narrowed.
answers.sourcing_note: LeyChile gives the final consolidated DL 1.094 and DS 597 with notes on each amending norm; the articles involved carry no amendment notes for 2000-2020. Point-in-time versions were not opened separately.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The 2020 'No' holds. The citation the MRD wrote for 2023 does not support its 2023 'Yes': art. 21 of Ley 21.325 is a due-process clause ('Debido proceso. El Estado asegurará a los extranjeros la igual protección...') and says nothing about confiscating documents.
answers.notes: Decreto 296/2022 art. 177 was not read. It dates from after 2020 and does not affect the past answers.

answers_by_date.basis: Ley 4.808 art. 3 No. 1 requires registration of 'los nacimientos que ocurran en el territorio de cada comuna'. Art. 28 sets a 60-day deadline and art. 29 lists who must request registration, with no reference to nationality or status. Ley 19.477 art. 4 No. 2 makes registering births a function of the Registro Civil. No practice source for 2000 itself. Registry data from 2001 on show children of irregular migrants were registered, though annotated 'hijo de extranjero transeúnte'.

The same provisions apply, unchanged. Registry figures (2,841 children registered as 'hijo de extranjero transeúnte', 2001-2014) show registration took place. The annotation concerned nationality, not registration itself.
Unchanged law. The CMW (2011) notes that children of parents in an irregular situation 'are recorded in the official register', annotated as children of foreigners in transit.

Unchanged law. SRCeI Resolución Exenta 3207 (August 2014) and Resolución 3509 (October 2014) limited the 'transeúnte' annotation to children of tourists or crew. This changed the nationality recorded, not the duty to register.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

answers.sourcing_note: In the consolidated Ley 4.808 on LeyChile, arts. 3 No. 1, 28 and 29 carry no amendment notes after 2000. The Ley 19.477 art. 4 amendments shown (Ley 20.711 of 2014, Ley 21.334 of 2021) concern apostilles, not birth registration. Practice evidence for 2000-2005 is indirect: registry data for 2001-2014 published in 2014.
answers.notes: The 'transeúnte' annotation (in use until 2014, and the subject of Corte Suprema nationality claims) goes to the right to nationality, not to registration. The Supreme Court rulings were not read, and none is relied on.

answers_by_date.basis: DL 1.094 art. 5 defines the visa as a permit stamped in the passport. Art. 8 requires it to record 'la clase de visa'. Art. 53 requires a cédula de identidad valid for the length of the visa. DS 597 arts. 10, 11, 103 and 108 implement these rules. Work authorisation follows from the visa class (DL 1.094 art. 74). No practice evidence for this period; the rating carries forward the 2020 level.

Same provisions. DTO 2910 (D.O. 23.05.2000) amended DS 597 arts. 40 and 86 on renewing work-contract visas and on permanent residence, without changing the duty to issue documents. No practice evidence.

Same provisions; Ley 20.430 came after this date. The CMW (2011) reports border officials arbitrarily refusing to stamp passports on entry, which later hampered regularisation. That is a documented gap in issuing status documents.

Same provisions. Decreto 1930 (D.O. 07.03.2015) came after this date and only changed the registration procedure. Ley 20.430 (2010) gives refugees a residence visa. The rating rests on the CMW 2011 findings; no later practice source was read.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

answers.sourcing_note: The amendment notes for DL 1.094 and DS 597 were read on LeyChile, but no point-in-time versions were opened. Practice evidence is thin: none for 2000 and 2005, and only the CMW 2011 findings for 2010 and 2015.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'Yes' holds. The 2020 'Effectively Always' rating looks generous given the documented passport-stamping problems (2011) and the widely reported processing delays at the DEM in 2018-2019; I did not read a source on the delays.
answers.notes: Documents covered only migrants holding a visa or permit; irregular migrants had none until regularised. The 2010 and 2015 ratings differ from 2000 because of documented practice, not because of any change in law.

answers_by_date.basis: Neither DL 1.094 nor DS 597 makes it an offence to destroy a migrant's documents. Código Penal art. 242 punishes only public employees who destroy documents entrusted to them. Art. 194, read with art. 193 No. 8, punishes a private person who hides an official document to the harm of another, but not destruction as such. Kept as 'No' per the starting answer. No practice evidence.
No change to Código Penal arts. 193, 194 or 242, or to the migration rules. No practice evidence.
No change. Ley 20.430 (April 2010) creates no such offence.
No change. Ley 20.507 (2011) creates no offence of destroying documents.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been no right protections neither in 2000 nor in 2020

events.what_changed: Applies Código Penal arts. 193-194 to falsehood in obtaining a Rol Único Nacional. It does not ban destroying documents, and it is after the period covered.
events.passage: El que cometiere falsedad en la solicitud, tramitación y/u otorgamiento del Rol Único Nacional en los términos previstos en los artículos 193 y 194 del Código Penal será castigado con las penas previstas en dichas normas

answers.repealed_search: Read Código Penal arts. 193, 194 and 242 and their amendment notes, and the infraction articles of DL 1.094 (arts. 68-77) and DS 597. No provision against destroying migrants' documents was found to have existed and then been repealed between 2000 and 2020. The relevant Código Penal articles carry no amendment notes for 2000-2020.
answers.sourcing_note: Código Penal amendment notes were read on LeyChile. No practice evidence was found for any date.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'No' is questionable. Código Penal art. 194 ('El particular que cometiere en documento público o auténtico alguna de las falsedades designadas en el artículo anterior'), read with art. 193 No. 8 ('Ocultando en perjuicio del Estado o de un particular cualquier documento oficial'), and art. 242 (public employees who 'sustraiga o destruya documentos') are of the same kind as the Argentine and Peruvian provisions the instrument codes 'Yes'. They applied unchanged throughout 2000-2020. A recoder might code 'Yes' for every date; I did not change the answer, because nothing changed in the period.
answers.notes: The general criminal-damage provisions were not read and are not cited.
